content:
alan: Heads-up — customers hitting runtime errors when importing @redwood/inference inside Cloudflare Workers. stack shows require("buffer") and fs access on module eval.

rachel: That's because the published CJS bundle pulls node modules. Workers don't have node APIs.

sam: Quick plan: publish a worker-targeted ESM build (dist/sdk.workers.mjs), add a package.json exports entry, and avoid any Buffer/require usage in that build.

mia: Typings: produce a separate d.ts for workers and add tsconfig.workers.json with lib ["es2020","webworker"]. Ensure our types don't reference node.

alan: For runtime-safe code use TextEncoder/TextDecoder and globalThis.crypto.subtle. Small helper: `const encode = s => new TextEncoder().encode(s)` and `const isEdge = typeof process === 'undefined' && typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function'`.

sam: CI: add a Miniflare smoke job that installs the package and attempts to import the workers bundle. That'll catch regressions.

ci-bot: opened issue #2345: "edge-build: worker ESM bundle + edge typings" and assigned to @sam.

alan: I'll update quickstart and docs to explain worker entrypoints + migration notes for 0.12 -> 0.13.

rachel: Sounds good — small release checklist please to avoid reintroducing node deps.
